main_text.p: lier pulchra & fatua: vel infulfa, quæ carot prudentia, vel cotumax fermone, vel, die vn⁠züchtige geßärden hat. Ein schön Weib ohn zucht/ist wie ein sau mit einem güldnen harband. ὥσπερ ἐν [illegible, ~10 letters] χρυσ[?] ἐν [illegible, ~8 letters], οὕτως γυναικὶ [illegible, ~12 letters] Vt enim fus monile foedat in luto, ita quoque stulta mulier abutitur pulchritudine fua, vt verè plumbeus gladius fit in aurea vagina, ficut in prouerbio dicitur: vel in eburnea vagina, quemadmodum Diogenes loquitur. Audiens enim adolescentem honesta specie, verbis parum honestis vtentem, Non te pudet, inquit, qui ex eburnea vagina plumbeum educas gladium? Ebur enim olim in summo erat precio. Dedecet ergo mulierem stultitia, imprudentia, impudentia, immodestia, socordia. Neque refert illam quidem esse pulchram & formosam, carere autem sapientia, destitui iudicio ratio nis, abuti pulchritudine, nec reputare qua ratione, & ad quem vsum naturale hoc donum à Deo susceperit. Fallax enim est gratia, & vana est pulchritudo: mulier timens Dominum, ipsa laudabitur, Prou. vlt. Forma bonum fragile est: & ob id non valde appetendum, neque in eo gloriandum. Qui pulchritudinem corporis diligit (D. Bernardo teste Serm. 64. de modo bene viuendi ad foro⁠rem) semetipsum decipit. Quare? quia pulchritudo corporis fallax est, vana est, terra & cinis est, deceptio est hominis. Antisthenes Atheniensis, cuidam adolescenti, qui curarat sese

page.notes: The Greek phrase is set in small italic type and is only partly legible; the bracketed parts are not read. The black letter German words are uncertain in places, especially "geßärden" and "güldnen". The first line is broken across the top, and "vel, die vn-" is cut at the line end; the page begins mid-sentence. The catchword "fefe" is uncertain. The "166" page number and "CONCIONES" running head are read from a stylised print. Edge marks at the left and right margins are not printed text and were left out.
